indicators.note: lost tells us the Conservative letter goes missing from the support word

parts.note: backing is support, as for a cause

explanation.surface: A political party loses the backing of a warm supporter.
explanation.definitionFit: A baking day is a hot one, so the word is an informal way of saying extremely warm.

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece placed on another sits above it, so it comes first

parts.note: a sun is a star
ling is another name for common heather

explanation.surface: A bird basks in the sunshine perched on a heather moor.
explanation.walkthrough: LING is a less familiar name for heather, common on British moorland.
explanation.definitionFit: The starling is a common speckled songbird, famous for its huge wheeling flocks.

clue.text: One can't know why the votes aren't counted!

definitions.meaning: an idiom for something impossible to predict
tellers count the votes in Parliament, so with no tellers present nobody does the counting

explanation.surface: An exasperated remark about an election where the ballots were never tallied.
explanation.walkthrough: In the House of Commons, tellers are the members who count votes in a division.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom expresses uncertainty: nobody can predict or say for sure what will happen.

indicators.note: in says the clairvoyance letters sit inside the ceremony word

parts.note: a rite is a ceremony
ESP, extrasensory perception, covers clairvoyance

explanation.surface: A psychic interlude holds up a solemn ritual.
explanation.definitionFit: A respite is a reprieve or postponement, a pause before something unpleasant resumes.

indicators.note: irregular means out of order, so the letters of these two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A dodgy wager lands a senior government figure in trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of the cabinet are the senior figures of a government, so they lead politically.

clue.text: Naughty child brings sin into prominence

indicators.note: into says the sin word goes inside the prominence word

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill, a prominence in the landscape
to err is to sin or do wrong

explanation.surface: A badly behaved child makes wrongdoing very noticeable.
explanation.walkthrough: A TOR is a rocky hilltop, common on Dartmoor in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: A little terror is an affectionate idiom for a mischievous, unruly youngster.

clue.text: Price of round and capacious cups?

parts.note: O is round in shape
DD is a large bra cup size, so roomy cups are DDs

explanation.surface: A cheeky question about what generously sized cups cost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cups' looks like drinking vessels but means bra cups.
explanation.definitionFit: In betting, the odds offered are the price on a horse or outcome.

definitions.meaning: the full set of actors in a play or film

explanation.surface: A throw meant for every member of the team.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: casting a line is throwing it, and actors in a production form the company.

indicators.note: pulled from says the student letter is taken out of the cavity word

parts.note: a hole is a cavity
L is a learner, the plate on a learner driver's car

explanation.surface: A weed is yanked out of a hole by a student gardener.
explanation.definitionFit: To hoe is to clear weeds by cutting them with a garden tool, so it is a verb for weeding.

parts.note: to age is to mature

indicators.note: complex means intricate or mixed, so the letters of and are jumbled

explanation.surface: A grown-up and complicated timetable.
explanation.definitionFit: An agenda is the list of items planned for a meeting, a programme of business.

clue.text: Glass we might raise to ourselves?

definitions.text: Glass we might raise to ourselves?

parts.words: Glass we might raise to ourselves?
parts.note: raising a glass usually means a toast, but this glass is held up to see our own reflection

explanation.surface: A toast we might drink in our own honour.
explanation.definitionFit: A looking-glass is held up so we can see ourselves reflected in it.

indicators.note: about says the written work goes round the border word

parts.note: prose is ordinary written work, as opposed to verse
a rim is a border or edge

explanation.surface: An essay written about a garden border plant.
explanation.definitionFit: The primrose is a pale yellow spring flower, a common woodland plant.

clue.text: Not natural to be a whisky hater?

definitions.meaning: contrary to one's inclination, an idiom from cutting wood across its fibres
someone opposed to grain whisky would be anti that grain spirit

explanation.surface: Is it unnatural to dislike whisky?
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes something that goes contrary to one's natural instinct or habit.

clue.text: When one replaces article, all is not well

indicators.note: replaces says the one letter takes the place of the article letter in the word all

parts.note: taken as written; that its letters with the next word read backwards spell the answer is a coincidence, not a hidden reversal
A is the indefinite article
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A grammar rule: swapping one word for another means everything is not fine.
explanation.definitionFit: Being ill is being unwell or sick, the opposite of healthy.

indicators.note: devouring says the monster swallows the old letter, holding it inside

parts.note: a dragon is a fire-breathing monster

explanation.surface: A fire-breathing beast swallows a veteran warrior.
explanation.definitionFit: A dragoon was a mounted infantryman, and the title survives in some cavalry regiments.

definitions.meaning: a dull, fixed habit one gets stuck in
the mating season of deer and other animals

explanation.surface: A routine schedule for when animals get busy.
explanation.definitionFit: A groove of habit is a dreary routine, and the same word names the season when stags mate.

clue.text: Engaging question from one lacking confidence?

definitions.meaning: friendly and pleasant, winning people over
an unsure person might ask whether they are capable, split as three words

explanation.surface: A charming question asked by someone full of self-doubt.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as 'AM I ABLE?', the answer is the anxious question of someone unsure of themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: An amiable person is friendly and good-natured, which makes them engaging company.

clue.text: Sailor surest to develop beyond comprehension

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is a sailor

indicators.note: to develop means to change and grow, so the letters of surest are rearranged

explanation.surface: A sailor's confident certainty grows into something baffling.
explanation.definitionFit: Something abstruse is obscure and hard to understand, so it lies past easy grasp.

parts.note: A is an abbreviation for advanced, as in A level
tissue is thin soft paper

explanation.surface: A cutting-edge paper is up for debate.
explanation.definitionFit: A matter that is the point in question is one currently being debated or disputed.

clue.text: Dean intends to be awkward in last romantic occasion

indicators.note: in says the jumbled letters go inside the last word

parts.note: to stay is to last or endure
a dean, or dene, is a narrow wooded valley, so another word for it is vale

indicators.note: awkward means clumsy or difficult, so the fodder letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A college dean plans to make trouble at the final romantic event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dean' looks like a college official but is a valley (VALE); 'to be awkward' jumbles VALE with INTENDS to give VALENTINESD, which goes 'in' STAY.
explanation.definitionFit: February 14th is the day for cards and gifts between lovers, the archetypal romantic date.

clue.text: As and When You Like by Shakespeare?

parts.note: by means at, as in waiting by or at the door
Will is William Shakespeare's first name

explanation.surface: A title spoof of the Shakespeare comedy As You Like It.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something whenever one chooses is doing it as one pleases, the phrase meaning freely.

clue.text: Fuss about an American soldier moving very slowly

indicators.note: about says the fuss word wraps round the other pieces

parts.note: ado is fuss or bother
a is the indefinite article, a version of an
GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A commotion surrounds a sluggish American trooper.
explanation.definitionFit: In music the tempo marking means slow and leisurely, slower than andante.

parts.note: struts look like supports holding up a stage, but are models strutting up and back along a raised runway

explanation.surface: A description of raised stages propped up by braces.
explanation.definitionFit: Fashion shows use a raised runway on which models walk out and back.

indicators.note: in says the answer sits inside the letters of laryngeal torment

explanation.surface: A vocalist suffering agony in the throat.
explanation.definitionFit: An alto is a singer with a low female or high male voice.

definitions.meaning: someone hilarious, as in 'she's a real hoot'

explanation.surface: A funny person makes others howl with laughter.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally a very funny person is a riot, and to shriek with mirth is the same verb.

indicators.note: around says the jumbled stone letters surround the lake letter
cracked means broken, so the letters of stone are rearranged

explanation.surface: A heated rock splits open beside a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Hot is slang for taken unlawfully, as in hot goods passed on by a fence.

clue.text: Yorkshire banker in ancient city close to Cumae

parts.note: Ur was an ancient city of Mesopotamia

indicators.note: close to means the end of, taking the final letter of Cumae

explanation.surface: A Yorkshire financier visiting an ancient site near Cumae.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banker' looks like a financier but is a river; Cumae was an ancient Greek city in Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: A banker in crosswords is a river, something with banks; the Ure flows through North Yorkshire.

indicators.note: knocked over means upended, so the beer word is read backwards

parts.note: Pils is a pilsner lager beer

explanation.surface: Someone stumbles and spills their pint.
explanation.definitionFit: To slip is to lose one's footing and fall or nearly fall.
